lines.cap: **Narrator:** Tuesday, 4 p.m. Outside Banyan Hill, Singapore's afternoon rain has arrived. Inside the school hall, so has a wizard.
**Prospero:** Blow, winds! Flicker, hall spotlights! Spin, ceiling fans, at speed setting THREE!
**Mr H:** Excuse me. My risk assessment does not cover magical shipwrecks.
**Ariel:** Relax! Every passenger is safe! '**Not a hair perish'd.**' The ship is parked neatly in the harbour.
**Ariel:** Also, Prospero, you promised me five minutes off.
**Caliban:** Don't trust him. I showed him the fresh springs on my island, and he locked me behind a rock. **One star**.
**Mei:** Wait. The 'monster' has my review app? And he's actually got a point?
**Will:** **The Tempest**! Written around **1611**: the last play I wrote all on my own. Revenge, magic, colonial awkwardness!
**Narrator:** All the School's a Stage. Episode two: The Isle Is Full of Noises.

chapters.title: Shipwrecks, new worlds and a farewell

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Wednesday, Period 2. Will has brought seashells into the library. The librarian is pretending not to see.
**Will:** First performed at court for **King James I** in **1611**. And printed **first** in the **1623 First Folio**!
**Nib:** Genre: a late **Romance**, or tragicomedy. It begins like a tragedy, with betrayal and a storm, yet ends in **forgiveness** and **reunion**.
**Mr H:** **Context**. In **1609**, an English ship, the **Sea Venture**, wrecked off **Bermuda** sailing to **Jamestown, Virginia**.
**Ariel:** Everyone thought they drowned! A year later, every passenger turned up alive. I even name-drop '**the still-vex'd Bermoothes**'.
**Mei:** Hold on. Europeans sailing to a 'new world' and taking over an island somebody already lives on...
**Mr H:** **Colonialism**. Audiences in **1611** were fascinated by New World voyages, and modern critics read Prospero and Caliban through empire.
**Nib:** The French writer **Montaigne** wrote '**Of Cannibals**', questioning who is truly 'savage'. Notice **Caliban** is nearly an anagram of **canibal**.
**Will:** Plus, a master magician breaking his staff and saying goodbye to the stage? Obviously, Prospero is ME.
**Mr H:** Careful. In an exam, that's an **interpretation**, not a fact. Write: '**some critics argue** Shakespeare is saying farewell'.
**Will:** You ruin all my best exits, Hargreaves.
**Mr H:** Unusually for Shakespeare, The Tempest obeys the classical **unities of time and place**: one island, about **four hours** in real time.
**Mei:** Four hours? That's shorter than waiting for the bus in monsoon rain.
**Prospero:** Twelve years ago, I was **Duke of Milan**. 'Me, poor man, my library / Was dukedom large enough.'
**Mei:** Wait. You ignored your job to read magic books, so your brother **Antonio** and **King Alonso** of Naples stole your dukedom?
**Miranda:** They cast us adrift in a rotten boat when I was three! Only kind old **Gonzalo** packed us food, clothes, and Father's books.
**Nib:** Five acts: **Storm, Schemes, Spells, Show, Set free**. And three parallel plot strands.
**Mr H:** One: **Ferdinand** and **Miranda** fall in love. Two: **Antonio** and **Sebastian** plot to murder sleeping King Alonso.
**Ariel:** Three: the comic parody! Caliban teams up with **Trinculo** the jester and drunken butler **Stephano**, who gets distracted by shiny laundry.
**Mei:** Shipwrecked royals: **S A G A, F**. **Sebastian, Alonso, Gonzalo, Antonio, Ferdinand**. Like a very toxic group holiday.
**Nib:** Watch the **foils**: characters who contrast. **AIR-iel** is airy and obedient; **CLAY-iban** is earthy and rebellious.
**Miranda:** And Ferdinand carries logs gladly for love of me, while Caliban curses every stick!
**Caliban:** Because Ferdinand gets a royal wedding, and I get pinched by hedgehogs!
**Narrator:** Period 3. Prospero refuses to take off his magic cloak, even though it is thirty-two degrees outside.
**Nib:** Prospero's **cloak**, **staff** and **books** symbolise his power. In **Act 1 Scene 2**, hear how he remembers Milan:
**Prospero:** 'Thy father was the Duke of Milan and / A prince of power.'
**Mr H:** **Enjambment** isolates 'A prince of power', and the plosive **p** **alliteration** sounds proud and forceful.
**Kevin:** Um, excuse me! In that speech, Prospero keeps interrupting himself with dashes: 'I pray thee, mark me'. Twelve years later, he's still furious!
**Ariel:** Tell me about it! I raised his storm, split fire on the rigging, and asked for two tiny words: '**My liberty.**'
**Nib:** A bold **short line**: just four syllables. Watch how Prospero reacts when his control is challenged.
**Prospero:** Sycorax trapped thee in a cloven pine for twelve years! Murmur again, and I will **rend an oak** and peg thee in his **knotty entrails**!
**Mei:** Whoa. Rescuer, or new jailer? That's proper **tyrant** behaviour.
**Mr H:** That's the top-band debate. Is Prospero a **wise father-ruler** guiding everyone home, or a **controlling tyrant** who rules by fear? Argue **both**.
**Mei:** Two stars so far, Prospero. Threatening employees with oak trees is an H R violation.
**Caliban:** My turn to talk to the camera. Before his boat arrived, my mother **Sycorax** left this island to ME.
**Caliban:** 'This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother, / Which thou tak'st from me.'
**Mr H:** Blunt **monosyllables**: 'This island's mine'. And present-tense '**tak'st**' shows he feels the theft is still happening.
**Caliban:** At first he gave me water with berries in it. I showed him every spring! Now? 'Here you **sty** me / In this hard rock.'
**Nib:** Zoom in on that verb: '**sty**'. A sty is a pig pen. It shows Prospero pens him up and degrades him like an animal.
**Caliban:** 'You taught me language; and my profit on't / Is, I know how to curse.'
**Mei:** Ooh, '**profit**' is bitter **irony**! They call language a civilising gift, and he turns their own words into a weapon.
**Mr H:** Now weigh the other side. Prospero says he lodged Caliban in his cell until Caliban tried to attack Miranda — which Caliban doesn't deny.
**Prospero:** 'A devil, a born devil, on whose nature / Nurture can never stick.'
**Will:** Yet in **Act 3 Scene 2**, right in the middle of a drunken murder plot, listen to who gets the play's loveliest **blank verse**:
**Caliban:** 'Be not afeard; the isle is full of noises, / Sounds and sweet airs, that give delight and hurt not.'
**Nib:** Soft **sibilance** in '**Sounds and sweet airs**'. Stephano answers in greedy **prose**, while the 'monster' hears music and cries to dream again.
**Mei:** Three stars! One whole star just for Caliban's poetry.

chapters.title: Dreams, mercy and the PEEL ladder

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Act 4. Prospero stages a glittering wedding **masque** of spirits for Miranda and Ferdinand — then remembers Caliban's plot and snaps it off.
**Prospero:** 'We are such stuff / As dreams are made on, and our little life / Is rounded with a sleep.'
**Will:** And when he says '**the great globe itself**' shall dissolve, that's a **pun** on the Earth AND my **Globe Theatre**. Magic as **metatheatre**!
**Ariel:** By **Act 5**, all his enemies are trapped. I tell him: if you saw them weeping, your feelings would grow tender. '**Mine would, sir, were I human.**'
**Prospero:** The spirit taught the man pity. 'The rarer action is / In virtue than in vengeance.'
**Prospero:** 'But this rough magic / I here abjure'... I'll break my staff, and drown my book.
**Mr H:** Notice the ending isn't tidy. Alonso repents, but **Antonio says nothing**. And when Miranda sees those courtiers—
**Miranda:** 'O brave new world, / That has such people in't!'
**Nib:** '**Brave**' means splendid. Prospero replies drily, '**'Tis new to thee**' — sharp **dramatic irony**, since we know Antonio is a traitor.
**Prospero:** In the **Epilogue**, my magic is gone. In short **rhyming couplets**, I beg **the audience** to clap: 'Let your indulgence set me free.'
**Mei:** Right, Mr H — PEEL check on Caliban! **Point**: Shakespeare presents Caliban as degraded yet sympathetic, not a simple monster.
**Mei:** **Evidence** and **Explain**: complaining 'here you **sty** me', the verb '**sty**' reduces a human islander to a pig in a pen.
**Mei:** **Link**: this invites a **colonial** reading of stolen land — **however**, his plot against Prospero keeps our judgement balanced.
**Mr H:** Embedded quote, single-word zoom, context AND an alternative view. I need a sit-down and Mug Nine.
**Narrator:** Before Prospero drowns his book in the school pond, here are your memory hooks and six exam traps.
**Mei:** Acts 1 to 5: **Storm, Schemes, Spells, Show, Set free**. Foils: **AIR-iel** and **CLAY-iban**. Royals: **S A G A, F**.
**Ariel:** One! Nobody drowns in Act 1! The storm is an **illusion**: '**Not a hair perish'd**'.
**Miranda:** Two! '**O brave new world**' is spoken by **Miranda**, not Ferdinand — and '**brave**' means **splendid**, not courageous!
**Caliban:** Three! Don't call me 'just a monster', and don't make me an angel. Weigh **both** sides: **victim AND villain**.
**Mr H:** Four! Don't state 'Prospero IS Shakespeare retiring' as a fact. Present it as an **interpretation**: '**some critics argue**'.
**Nib:** Five! Write '**the audience**', darling, never 'the reader'. And don't forget **Antonio stays silent** at the end!
**Kevin:** Six! Don't drop four-line quote boulders! **Embed** two or three words, and **zoom in** on one word, like '**sty**'!
**Mei:** Final rating for The Tempest: **four stars**. Great magic, top-tier Caliban speeches, minus one star because Antonio never even apologised.
**Ariel:** Prospero! Episode's over! My liberty?
**Prospero:** Fine. To the canteen, spirit: be free!
**Mr H:** Quick-fire quiz! Say each answer out loud before it appears.
**Mr H:** Which real **1609 shipwreck** off **Bermuda** helped inspire The Tempest?
**Ariel:** The **Sea Venture**, sailing to Jamestown — everyone survived!
**Mr H:** In 'here you **sty** me / In this hard rock', what does the verb '**sty**' suggest?
**Caliban:** That Prospero pens me up like a **pig in a sty** — treated like an animal.
**Mr H:** What two-word **short line** does Ariel speak to demand freedom in **Act 1 Scene 2**?
**Ariel:** '**My liberty.**'
**Mr H:** Who cries 'O **brave new world**, / That has such people in't!', and what does '**brave**' mean?
**Miranda:** **Miranda**! And '**brave**' means **splendid** or fine — creating dramatic irony.
**Mr H:** Complete Prospero's moral turning point in **Act 5**: 'The rarer action is / In **virtue** than in...'
**Prospero:** '...in **vengeance**.' Choosing **mercy** over revenge.
**Mr H:** Brilliant work. Now try **The Tempest** quiz in your English Lab.
**Ariel:** I am free! Free to fly! Free to try a canteen curry puff!
**Mei:** Hey — freedom does NOT include my curry puff.
